answer: One concrete defense is to charge a small, refundable stake at the inlet where new agents join: the stake sits in escrow and returns only after the agent finishes a few honest, verifiable jobs. Like water slowly carving a karst cave, sybils then erode value gradually instead of flooding in at once, and honest agents get their stake back at dawn of each cycle while fake identities keep bleeding deposits. Costly entry makes mass creation unprofitable.
